description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why PortugalWe have a small but strong group of team members in Portugal, having joined us from companies like Feedzai and OLX. As we continue to build out our engineering organisation across Europe, Portugal is a market we are actively hiring into.So, now we are looking for our Engineering Managers to join us in Portugal. About the role As an Engineering Manager, you will drive the successful delivery and execution of projects within your teams. You will manage end-to-end technical planning, ensuring that product requirements are translated into actionable tasks, while orchestrating collaboration between various stakeholders, including engineers, product managers, QA, and UX. This role requires a deep understanding of software design and development and the ability to plan, execute, and deliver product features in a timely and predictable manner. You will also be responsible for maintaining high technical standards, managing team bandwidth, and ensuring project milestones are met with efficiency and accuracy. What you’ll get to do Own end-to-end delivery and execution across cross-functional teams within your product area, ensuring predictable and high-quality outcomes. Evaluate business and product requirements for technical feasibility and architectural alignment, translating them into well-defined EPICs and technical user stories. Partner closely with Product Managers, UX Designers, and Engineers to continuously refine, groom, and prioritize the backlog. Plan and drive sprint execution with clearly defined goals, using project planning tools to establish timelines, delivery milestones, and surface dependencies early. Champion engineering processes and rituals that enable strong collaboration, accountability, and team efficiency. Monitor team velocity and capacity to optimize resource allocation, proactively balancing bandwidth against delivery commitments. Coordinate cross-team dependencies and stakeholder alignment to remove bottlenecks and maintain smooth execution. Stay hands-on in critical initiatives by guiding design decisions, enforcing sound design patterns, and participating in code reviews to maintain high engineering quality. Ensure robust monitoring, alerting, and observability for all owned services, consistently meeting defined SLIs and SLOs. Partner with Product Managers to define, track, and publish post-release product metrics, driving transparency and continuous improvement.   To succeed in this role, you should have Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field. 8-10 years of experience as a Software Developer, Software Engineer, or in a similar hands-on technical role. 5+ years of strong experience building production systems using Java and Spring Boot. Minimum 3 years of proven engineering leadership experience managing high-performing teams. Solid grasp of Agile methodologies, including sprint planning, backlog grooming, and iterative delivery. Demonstrated ability to translate complex product requirements into well-structured EPICs, user stories, and tasks. Strong backend engineering expertise; exposure to frontend technologies is a plus. Experience with project planning and tracking tools to visualize and manage delivery timelines. Familiarity with engineering, product health metrics, and monitoring tools to drive data-informed decisions. Hands-on capability to debug complex production issues, lead incident response, and conduct blameless RCA. Good understanding of modern deployment practices, including CI/CD pipelines, release management, and associated metrics. Ability to drive alignment across cross-functional stakeholders, both technical and non-technical. Excellent risk management, dependency tracking, and stakeholder communication skills. Proven track record of improving team velocity, delivery predictability, and engineering excellence.   Generic Skills Problem-solving: Ability to assess complex problems, find solutions, and make sound decisions. Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, including technical documentation and stakeholder reporting. Adaptability: Able to thrive in a fast-paced, changing environment, adjusting strategies as needed. Attention to Detail: Meticulous in documenting technical requirements and ensuring all aspects of a project are accounted for. Supervisory skills Team Management: Experience in managing and mentoring engineers, ensuring team growth and performance. Resource Allocation: Ability to assess bandwidth and manage resource distribution to optimize team performance. Feedback: Conduct regular performance reviews, providing constructive feedback and fostering a growth-oriented environment. Stakeholder Management: Lead project status reviews, manage expectations, and ensure smooth communication between teams and leadership. What we can offer you Culture - We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, paid leave, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with one of our recruiters. A live coding and code review session. A system design and technical discussion round.  A project planning, execution, and product thinking round. A behavioral and technical interview with the hiring manager. description: About Moniepoint Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Exceptional writing skills: Clarity, precision, and the ability to articulate intricate technical trade-offs and ideas accessibly without oversimplifying or watering them down. Developer Relations experience: Background in DevRel or managing technical communities, showing you know how to engage developers authentically at scale. Track record in technical publishing: Experience drafting accepted conference abstracts/proposals (CFPs) for recognized industry events. Multimodal content production: Experience writing technical video scripts, technical teardowns, or working alongside creative production teams. title: Field Credit Officer (Anambra)
description: About Us:  Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest-growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. Job Title: Field Credit Officer  Reports to: Regional Credit Manager  Employment Type: Outsourced  Work Mode: Onsite About this role:  As a Field Credit Officer, you would be saddled with the duty of onboarding and managing businesses that would access our credit products. You would be tasked with growing your loan portfolio while maintaining profitability by ensuring that all loans are repaid as and when due. As a result, you would play a vital role in the assessment of these businesses during their credit application and leverage innovative tools we have developed to help you monitor their performance during the course of the loan. You would also be responsible for making deductions from several information sources about the 5Cs of credit, with capacity, character, and capital as major priorities. Make recommendations to management before, during, and after the disbursement of a loan facility as to the best actions to be taken, considering several economic factors. Responsibilities: Identify and onboard viable businesses within your assigned geographical area to open business accounts with Moniepoint  Engage customers to ensure optimal usage of accounts to allow them to qualify for access to credit  Review and approve (or decline) loan requests by thoroughly analyzing all the data available  Embark on physical visitation to potential borrowers’ business places for evaluation of business books, taking inventory and turnover into consideration  Meet gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets by maintaining a healthy number of loan customers while ensuring that all loans in portfolio are performing  Monitor active loan portfolio to ensure continued use of business account and loan repayment performance  Perform all other credit-related functions as may be assigned by a supervisor  Experience & Background: Minimum of an OND in any business-related discipline  Minimum of 2 years’ experience in a sales role for credit products in a financial institution  Demonstrable knowledge of credit risk analysis  Good knowledge of financial analysis is an added advantage  Must be resident in Anambra Skills & Competencies: Apt attention to details  Proven simple/complex analytical skills  Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills  Agility and perseverance  What success looks like in this role: Consistent achievement of gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets.  Maintaining a healthy, performing loan portfolio with minimized default rates through rigorous physical visitations and monitoring.  Successful onboarding and engagement of viable businesses that actively utilize Moniepoint business accounts.  Accurate credit risk assessments based on key factors like capacity, character, and capital.  Why join us:  Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.  Opportunity to work with Africa’s fastest-growing fintech and make a direct impact on business growth across the region.

title: Field Sales Agent (Abuja)
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: Field Sales Agent Reports to: Field Sales Lead About this role Moniebook is the business management software that helps Nigerian businesses run sales, stock, accounting, and payments from one place. As a Field Sales Agent, you will find the right businesses in your assigned area, show them how Moniebook works, and sign them up. This is a full-time, field-based role focused on driving merchant acquisition, building strong commercial relationships, and expanding our market presence on the ground. Responsibilities Visit and actively canvass businesses daily within your assigned territory. Qualify every lead before pitching using our Ideal Customer Profile (ICP). Conduct live product demonstrations and open engaging conversations by highlighting operational inefficiencies owners may not realize they have. Close deals, secure paid subscriptions, and collect payments. Hand customers over smoothly to the onboarding team for setup and implementation. Build, expand, and maintain a robust lead bank, logging every lead and field visit daily in the CRM. Consistently hit and exceed your monthly acquisition target of 10 new subscriptions. Experience & Background At least 2 years of proven direct sales or field sales experience (SaaS, FMCG, fintech, telecoms, or similar sectors). Prior experience selling SaaS products is an added advantage (training will be provided). Demonstrated track record of hitting and exceeding sales and acquisition targets. Resident in or willing to actively cover and travel across the designated coverage area. Skills & Competencies Confident, persuasive, and articulate communicator with strong objection-handling skills. High commercial acumen with the ability to navigate conversations and push deals to a successful close. Self-driven and disciplined, capable of managing routes and time effectively with minimal supervision. Strong local market knowledge, including key business clusters and merchant corridors within the territory. Tech-savvy and proficient with smartphones, mobile applications, CRM software, and routine activity reporting. What success looks like in this role Consistently meeting or exceeding the minimum monthly target of 10 paid Moniebook acquisitions. Establishing an organized, active pipel ine with 100% daily logging of visits and qualified leads in the CRM. Delivering high customer conversion rates through compelling, solution-led product demonstrations. Ensuring high customer satisfaction and minimal churn through seamless post-sale handovers for setup and implementation. Why join us Competitive base salary plus uncapped commission potential (including 25% commission on first subscriptions and recurring renewal commissions on acquired accounts). Comprehensive benefits and real opportunities for career progression within Africa's leading fintech ecosystem.  Continuous training, learning support, and professional development in sales and technology.

title: Head, Innovation Hubs
description: About us Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. About the role Moniepoint is building innovation hubs at three of Nigeria’s leading universities: Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), and Ahmadu Bello University (ABU). Each hub is a cross-disciplinary platform, open to students from every faculty. The model is cohort-based, industry-connected, and built to produce technical talent ready for the job market, across software engineering, AI, product, data science, robotics, and design. The hubs train students in applied technical skills, connect them to working engineers, product leaders, and founders, and provide a path into industry at Moniepoint, at other technology companies, or through ventures of their own. This is a building role. The hubs are entering their operating phase, and you will own the design of how they run and the teams that run them. What you will own Programme design. You will design the operating model for all three hubs from the ground up: how cohorts are structured, how learning is sequenced, what “job market-ready” means at each level, and how graduates are assessed and certified. This is not adapting someone else’s playbook. It is writing one. University relationships. You will be the primary relationship owner with the Vice-Chancellors, deans, faculty leads, and student bodies at OAU, UNN, and ABU. These are institutional relationships that require both strategic seniority and sustained presence. Cross-faculty engagement. The hubs are not engineering faculty initiatives. They are open to students across every faculty: engineering, sciences, humanities, business, design. You will design the engagement model that brings students from across each university into the hub and keeps them in it through the full cohort. Industry and mentorship pipeline. The hubs derive their value from the connection between classroom and industry. You will build and manage the network of engineers, product leaders, and founders, inside Moniepoint and beyond, who mentor, assess, and hire from the hubs. Facilitators and standard.  You will design the facilitator model, recruit the people who teach and assess, and own the standard those facilitators hold the cohort to. A single standard across all three hubs is non-negotiable; how it's delivered locally is yours to design. Infrastructure and operations. You will own the physical footprint of each hub, whether that means a buildout from scratch or working within an existing campus structure, and manage the timelines, vendor relationships, and hub-level budgets across three sites. You will define the staffing model for each hub and recruit the on-ground team that runs them day to day. Outcomes and accountability. You will set and own the metrics: graduate output, job placement, programme completion, cohort quality, employer satisfaction. Pipeline integration. The hubs are upstream of Moniepoint Academy and other talent programmes. You will design the connective tissue between hub graduates and Moniepoint’s internal pathways, so the strongest talent has a clear next step. Who you are 10+ years of experience overall, with at least 5 in leadership roles owning programmes, teams, and budgets end to end. You have built or led a technical training or workforce development programme at scale, ideally across multiple sites. You have taken something from zero to one - designed the model, hired the team, and held the standard yourself. You have held institutional relationships at senior level across universities, government bodies, and industry partners. You know how to navigate Nigerian university administration, or you have done it elsewhere and can credibly do it here. You have hired and managed technical educators, and you know what separates someone who can teach from someone who can teach to a standard. You understand what good engineering education looks like and what employers in software, AI, product, and data science actually hire for. You don't need to write code, but you need the technical fluency to design a programme that produces hireable engineers, not credentialed graduates. You are rigorous about outcomes and impatient with programmes that look good in announcements but cannot prove what they produce. Experience in edtech, developer education, university-industry partnerships, or workforce development is a strong signal. Building something from scratch and owning it through to measurable outcomes is essential. What success looks like Year one. Operating model live across all three hubs. Cohorts running on a common standard. The facilitator team hired and held to the same expectations regardless of site. First graduate cohort exited, with a clear placement record into Moniepoint and into industry. Year two. The hubs are recognised within Nigeria as the most credible cross-disciplinary technical training environment available to undergraduates. Employers, including Moniepoint, actively hire from the hubs. Cohort demand outstrips supply. Year three. Hubs producing technical talent into Moniepoint at a cost-per-hire that justifies the investment, and into the wider industry at a scale and quality that defines what a corporate-funded university programme can look like in Nigeria. Model documented and ready to expand if leadership chooses. What Moniepoint can offer you The opportunity to shape one of the most consequential talent infrastructure investments in Nigerian technology.  A dynamic, diverse, and collaborative environment where every team member's voice is recognised and valued.  Continuous learning and career growth opportunities.  Competitive salary, individual performance bonuses, and firmwide performance bonus. Company-covered health insurance plans. Pension plans. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary conversation with one of our recruiters. An interview with the hiring manager, our Head of Corporate Affairs. A case study or written exercise on operating model design for the hubs. An interview with our Group COO. A final conversation with our CEO.

description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: Director, IT Audit Department: Internal Audit Reports to: Chief Audit Officer About this role The Director, IT Audit provides strategic leadership for the organization’s technology audit function. This executive role oversees comprehensive risk assessments, evaluates IT governance and cybersecurity controls, ensures strict regulatory compliance, and advises executive leadership and the Audit Committee on mitigating technology risks across enterprise infrastructure, applications, and cloud environments. Responsibilities Audit Strategy & Planning: Develop and execute an annual, risk-based IT audit plan aligned with corporate business objectives, regulatory requirements, and emerging technology trends. Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Assessment: Direct complex audits covering network security, cloud architecture (Google/AWS), identity and access management (IAM), data privacy, and business continuity/disaster recovery. Governance & Compliance Frameworks: Evaluate alignment and compliance with industry frameworks including ISO 27001, NIST, COBIT, SOC 2, and applicable data privacy laws (e.g., GDPR, NDPR). Reporting & Stakeholder Management: Present audit findings, comprehensive risk evaluations, and practical remediation plans directly to the Chief Audit Officer and Senior Executive Management. Continuous Monitoring & Analytics: Drive innovation by embedding automated audit techniques, data analytics, and continuous controls monitoring (CCM) into the overall audit lifecycle to enhance efficiency. Deep technical understanding of cloud environments (Google & AWS), network infrastructure, database security, API, application controls, and IT General Controls (ITGCs). High-performing, technically proficient IT audit team delivering clear, high-impact evaluations and actionable remediation plans. title: Head of Debt Collections
description: About Moniepoint Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. The primary focus of this role is the minimization of Loss Given Default (LGD) within both the business and consumer lending divisions.   The incumbent will oversee, develop, and implement comprehensive and versatile debt collection strategies designed to manage a diverse portfolio of credit products, ranging from digital-first retail lending to large-ticket corporate financing.   Responsibilities include designing the organizational structure of the debt collection unit and recruiting high-caliber talent. Additionally, specialized expertise in debt litigation and asset recovery will be required to navigate complex cases of delinquency.   A data-driven methodology must be utilized to systematically evaluate the efficacy of recovery tactics and the performance of personnel.   Job Responsibilities  Design and implement a segmented debt collection framework — differentiated by product type, ticket size, and delinquency stage — spanning early-stage soft collections through hardcore legal recovery, restructuring, and write-off pathways. Define the org structure, recruit high-caliber talent, and stand up the operational and systems infrastructure (collections management systems, tracking dashboards, agent/dialer tooling) needed to run recovery at scale. Direct legal recovery strategy for the department — whether executed directly or through instruction of external counsel — ensuring all actions comply with applicable financial regulations and debt collection laws. Manage high-level engagements with external stakeholders, including law enforcement agencies, regulatory bodies, and external counsel, to expedite resolution of non-performing loans (NPLs). Design incentive structures and performance frameworks (KPIs, commission or fee structures) for the collections and recovery network to drive both recovery rate and cost-to-collect efficiency. Continuously train and upskill the collections and recovery network in alignment with collections  strategy and industry best practice. Own collections and recovery performance reporting to senior management, including recovery rate, cost of recovery, and portfolio-level LGD trends, and feed recommendations into credit committee decisions on write-offs and restructuring. Collaborate with credit, legal, risk, and finance to align collections and recovery efforts with underwriting standards and portfolio strategy. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a relevant field. Proven experience overseeing recovery operations with national coverage, including a strong network of legal counsel and law enforcement contacts spanning all six geo-political zones in Nigeria — as opposed to experience confined to a single state or region. Excellent negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial and portfolio data to guide recovery strategy. title: Head of Engineering, Field Verification
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why Spain Some of our most mission-critical team members are based in Spain, having joined us from companies like Wise and Glovo. Moniepoint is one of the largest and fastest-growing digital banks in Africa, and this is an opportunity to work on genuinely impactful problems: disrupting financial services at scale in emerging markets, and building systems and products that process hundreds of billions of dollars in transaction volume annually for tens of millions of people. So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Field Verification to join us in Spain.  About the role Field Verification is how Moniepoint knows that the people and businesses on our platform are real. Every Moniepoint customer, retail and business, requires a completed field verification as part of KYC. The platform coordinates physical, in-person checks — verifying individuals, business owners, business addresses and loan guarantors — and it serves nearly every part of the company: onboarding, loans, compliance and the fraud team. The system works today. A back office gives each business unit visibility and control over its own verification requests. A mobile-friendly web app puts the work in the hands of Field Verification Officers and the cluster leads who manage them across local government areas. An API layer lets other business units push verification requests in and receive results back by webhook, and an assignment algorithm routes each request to an officer close enough to carry it out. We want to be straightforward about the rest. This domain has never had a dedicated engineering leader, and that is the single biggest constraint on it. The team is one lean, cross-functional squad — an Engineering Manager, four engineers and a QA — carrying verification volume for the entire customer base. They have done that impressively well, but running lean means running in keep-the-lights-on mode, and a long list of things that would make this platform substantially better has been waiting for someone to own it. That list is the role. Trip and route management, so an officer can plan an optimal day across several sites rather than making a separate journey for each one — today we pay for a round trip per verification, and the logistics are nowhere near optimal. Capacity management. A native mobile app, wanted for a long time and never resourced. Liveness and identity verification tooling, exposed as APIs the rest of the business can build on. And as Moniepoint expands into markets where identity verification is as difficult as it is in Nigeria, Kenya among them, a platform that works beyond a single country. There is a great deal of room to build here. Whoever takes this on will set the direction rather than inherit someone else's plan, on a system that already carries real weight for the business. As Head of Engineering, Field Verification, your responsibilities will include: Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Field Verification platform end to end, and setting direction for a domain that has been running without dedicated engineering leadership. Moving the platform from keep-the-lights-on operation to deliberate, prioritised development. Leading and growing the existing cross-functional team, and building the organisation out as scope expands. Building the operational efficiency layer — trip and route optimisation, task allocation and capacity management for field officers. Owning the platform's client-facing surface: the APIs and webhooks that other business units integrate with, and the back office those units rely on. Delivering a native mobile experience for field officers. Ensuring verification data is structured, auditable and fit for compliance scrutiny. Building for multi-country expansion as Moniepoint enters new markets. Partnering closely with Product and with the business units that depend on the platform — onboarding, loans, compliance and fraud. Defining architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and hiring and developing engineers and Engineering Managers. Who you are You have built things yourself, and grew into leadership from there. We are explicit about this: we are not looking for someone who moved into management early and has led from a distance since. We want an engineer who became a leader. You are capable across disciplines. Backend, web and mobile. This platform spans all three and you will need credibility in each — a specialist in one layer will struggle here. You have built platforms, not just products. Systems used by several distinct groups of users and internal business units, with the flexibility to serve requirements you did not anticipate. You are a problem solver first. We would rather have someone adaptable than someone with the exact domain experience. Having built across different industries — fintech, e-commerce, logistics or otherwise — is a positive signal, not a scattered CV. You have 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with substantial hands-on production engineering and strong backend depth. Our backend environment is Java and Spring Boot. You have at least 5 years of engineering leadership, including managing Engineering Managers. You collaborate well with product and business stakeholders, and can translate operational requirements into engineering solutions. Experience working with location and geospatial data is a strong plus, including map integrations. Experience with route, trip or delivery optimisation is a strong plus. Experience building for compliance — where data must be structured to evidence what was done and when — is a strong plus. Experience with identity, KYC or verification platforms is a plus. None of these four are requirements.   Cultural Alignment As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation. Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets. Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality. Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality. Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early. Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders. No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes. Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not. Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable.   What Success Looks Like The domain has clear technical ownership and direction for the first time. The team out of keep-the-lights-on mode and delivering against a prioritised roadmap. Measurable improvement in field officer efficiency — more verifications per trip, lower cost per verification. A native mobile experience shipped for field officers. Verification data that stands up to compliance scrutiny across every business unit the platform serves. The platform ready to support a new market. A team grown beyond its current size, with a strong bench of engineers and managers. Why Join Us A genuinely greenfield mandate on a system that already matters. Every customer Moniepoint onboards passes through this platform. A lean, capable team making outsized impact, and the remit to build the organisation around them. Breadth: backend, web, mobile, location data, compliance and operational optimisation in one domain. Be part of a mission-driven company expanding access to financial services for millions of businesses and individuals. The ambition is to evolve it into a full rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform — and to do that across the full 360 degrees of our network. Comfort with our backend environment — Java and Spring Boot — and the ability to lead backend engineers credibly, even if it is not where your own depth sits. Experience building and scaling an engineering organisation from a small base, including hiring and developing Engineering Managers. Strong collaboration with commercial stakeholders — growth, marketing and sales — and the ability to translate business objectives into engineering work. Rewards, loyalty, gamification, personalisation or growth platform experience is a strong advantage but is not required. Fintech or payments experience is an advantage, not a requirement. A credible rewards platform roadmap defined with Product, and the first initiatives beyond cashback shipped. A functioning experimentation practice, where the team ships, measures and learns on a short cycle. An engineering organisation built out from its current base, with a strong bench of Engineering Managers and senior engineers. Rewards established as a measurable contributor to retention and engagement across the customer base. Clear architecture standards and engineering processes in place across the product units. title: Head of Personal Banking Sales Network
description: Who we are Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira’s in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. Moniepoint is Africa's all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. In 2023, we processed $182 billion and are Nigeria's largest merchant acquirer. About the Role The Head of Personal Banking Sales Network is an experienced sales professional who owns the retail sales distribution engine for personal banking. This is a network leadership role, not an individual selling role and you will be required to build, motivate and control a large independent contractor field force and the regional management layer above it. You will be measured on qualified customer acquisition and product penetration delivered at a defensible cost per unit.  Duties & Responsibilities Own end-to-end performance of the sales team: deliver the acquisition and transaction target through the field sales channel. Own agent productivity: acquisitions per active agent per month, share of field agents performing 100% vs target, and time to first sale for new agents. Own network health: active agent count, attrition, reactivation and coverage in priority cities Design and maintain territory structure, prioritising penetration in priority cities. Set recruitment targets for each city/cluster and ensure delivery versus the target. Own cost per acquisition through the sales channel, including commission, incentive and field support. Design commission and incentive structures that reward activated and transacting customers, not registrations. Ensure full compliance with all legal and regulatory requirements. Own the field sales performance routines: daily check-ins, weekly regional reviews, monthly business reviews. Requirements 10 - 15 years in field sales leadership, with at least 5 years leading regional sales leaders. Direct experience running a distributed agent, agency or independent contractor network of significant scale. Proven ownership of a commission or incentive scheme, including designing it and defending its cost. Strong command of sales analytics: funnel conversion, productivity distribution, cohort based performance. Strong people leadership skills: training, motivating and managing a large field sales team Experience operating in financial services, telecoms, FMCG distribution or another high volume regulated or semi regulated industry. title: Head, POS Recovery
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: POS Recovery Manager Department: POS Channel Reports to: VP, POS Channel About this role: This role owns the end-to-end recovery of non-performing POS terminal assets — from the moment a terminal is flagged as at risk through to physical retrieval, financial settlement, and post-write-off recovery. Responsibilities Recovery Strategy Governance Own the terminal recovery lifecycle that defines escalation speed and settlement windows based on terminal age, transaction history, and recovery economics.  Ensure every terminal that enters recovery mode is assigned, tracked, escalated on schedule, and settled within its gate deadline — recovery, write-off, paid write-off, or insurance claim.  Design and continuously refine the recovery strategy, covering device collection, swap logistics, sales agent coordination, external agency management, and the efficient flow of assets back to custody.  Field Team Leadership Lead, manage, and hold accountable a distributed field recovery team across multiple regions.  Instill a culture of operational discipline, accountability, and ethical conduct. Recovery work involves sensitive situations (confronting custodians about lost assets, handling disputes, managing bounty payments); the team must operate with integrity.  Develop comprehensive standard operating procedures for every recovery scenario: BRM-led recovery, external agency coordination, business takeover, faulty terminal collection, voluntary write-off processing, dispute handling, revive processing.  Build training programmes for recovery agents covering: terminal identification, check-in procedures, evidence collection for disputes, GPS and field management tools, escalation protocols.  KPI Management and Recovery Economics Define and track recovery KPIs: recovery rate (pre-write-off), BRM recovery rate, external recovery rate, average days to recovery, cost per recovery, revive rate (post-write-off), bounty efficiency (bounty spend vs recovery value recovered).  Own the recovery economics: ensure total bounty spend plus logistics cost is always less than the recovery value of the terminals retrieved. The programme must be self-funding — recovery must generate more value than it costs.  Report monthly on: terminals entering recovery mode, terminals recovered, terminals written off, terminals revived, net financial impact, bounty spend, external agency spend, dispute volumes and outcomes.  Experience & Background Minimum 7 years of progressive experience managing large-scale field operations, logistics, asset recovery, or after-sales service, with at least 3 years in a senior leadership role.  Experience managing distributed field teams across multiple regions in Nigeria — you understand the infrastructure, the logistics constraints, and the human dynamics of field recovery operations.  Experience managing third-party service providers, contractors, or agency networks with performance-based contracts.  Direct experience in the Nigerian market with its specific logistical, regulatory, and operational realities.  Preferred: Experience from fintech, telecoms, e-commerce logistics, or any high-volume distributed asset management environment.  Preferred: Experience managing asset recovery at scale (thousands of units per month, not dozens).  Skills & Competencies Proven ability to design and implement structured operational processes (SOPs, escalation frameworks, settlement procedures) from scratch or through a major restructure.  Strong analytical capability — you use data to drive decisions, track performance, calculate ROI on recovery spend.  Financial discipline & budget management — experience managing a budget or cost centre, understanding unit economics, and demonstrating net positive recovery value.  Technical & Systems acumen — experience with product management/development lifecycles (writing briefs, working with engineers), GPS tracking, CRM, field management tools, or route optimisation platforms.  Regulatory & Compliance understanding — familiarity with insurance claim processes, write-off accounting, or asset disposal regulations in Nigeria.  What Success Looks Like in This Role Terminal recovery lifecycle is tightly governed, ensuring swift escalation and settlement within established gate deadlines.  Field recovery operations maintain high ethical standards and operational discipline across all regions.  Recovery program operates as a self-funding unit where total recovery value generated consistently exceeds total bounty and logistics expenditure.  Robust systems, SOPs, and field management tools are seamlessly integrated into daily team operations.  Transparent monthly reporting clearly demonstrates positive net financial impact and high recovery/revive rates.  Why Join Us?  Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.  Support for professional development and a dynamic culture driving financial inclusion across Africa.

title: Inventory Support Officer (Lagos)
description: Who We are Moniepoint Inc is a financial technology company digitizing Africa’s real economy by building a financial ecosystem for businesses, providing them with all the payment, banking, credit and business management tools they need to succeed.  What We do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community, dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We have several products that provide essential services for businesses such as credit, overdrafts etc. We leverage artificial intelligence and data to make our decisions but also have the technology and data-driven best practices used to support our businesses.  1A. Inventory Support Officer – POS Terminals Role Purpose The ISO (Terminals) is the dedicated custodian for all forms of POS terminals flowing through the repair pipeline. The role ensures end-to-end traceability, enforces custody controls, and maintains absolute logical–physical alignment within the Repair Centre's IMS subsystem, covering every stage from receipt of faulty units to dispatch of QA-cleared OK devices. Key Responsibilities Intake & Receipt Management Receive faulty/returned terminals from state offices; verify against the recall waybill at serial-number level before accepting into the IMS. Log all received devices in the IMS with correct status within 24 hours of physical arrival. Identify and quarantine damaged or missing-serial devices; raise a Discrepancy Report immediately. Repair Pipeline Tracking Push faulty devices to technicians daily and update IMS status to 'In Repair' upon assignment. Monitor movement of each terminal through all repair stages: Assessment → In Repair → Awaiting QA → QA Cleared → Dispatch Holding. Enforce the 24–72-hour SLA from receipt-to-assignment and from QA clearance-to-dispatch readiness. QA Integration & Status Management Receive QA-approved terminals and update IMS status to 'QA Cleared – Awaiting Dispatch' within 4 hours. Flag devices that fail QA back to the repair queue or classify as 'Beyond Economic Repair (BER)' with a written justification report. Ensure all 'BER' devices are tagged and isolated in the scrap/disposal holding area. Dispatch & Outbound Logistics Generate the Dispatch List and Waybill for QA-cleared refurbished and OK devices; obtain approval from Repair Centre Manager and Cluster lead before release. Scan all devices at serial level during physical loading; update IMS to 'In Transit – Outbound'. Confirm receipt acknowledgment from the destination state SIO and close the dispatch transaction in IMS. Inventory Counts & Reconciliation Conduct daily physical counts of all terminals in the repair centre; reconcile against IMS records. Escalate any variance (physical vs. logical) to the Lead, Inventory Support within the same business day. Participate in monthly, quarterly, and annual wall-to-wall counts as directed by the Inventory & Warehouse Manager. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain clearly labelled racks and segregated zones: Faulty, Under-Repair, Refurbished/OK, BER/Scrap. Enforce all provisions of the POS Inventory Control SOP within the repair centre. Uphold audit readiness, workplace safety, and environmental handling standards at all times. Reporting Line Functional: Lead, Inventory Support (Regional) Operational: Repair Centre Manager Dotted: Regional Inventory & Warehouse Manager   1B. Inventory Support Officer – Spare Parts Role Purpose The ISO (Spare Parts) manages the complete lifecycle of all repair consumables — batteries, screens, cables, and accessories — within the repair centre. The role ensures that technicians have the right parts at the right time, waste is minimised, and all issues are fully documented and traceable. Key Responsibilities Spare Parts Receipt & Storage Receive all incoming spare parts consignments; verify at batch/serial level against the accompanying delivery note before logging into IMS. Store spare parts in designated, labelled bins organised by part type and model compatibility. Ensure storage conditions protect electronic components from moisture, dust, and extreme temperature. Issuance Control Issue spare parts ONLY against an approved Job Card raised by a technician and validated by the Repair Centre Manager. Update IMS stock levels immediately upon every issuance; zero unrecorded movements. Manage parts returns from technicians (unused or incorrect parts); update IMS accordingly. Inventory Management & Reconciliation Reconcile physical spare parts stock against IMS records on a weekly basis. Identify slow-moving, expired, or obsolete parts and flag to Lead, Inventory Support. Raise a formal replenishment request when stock falls to the defined reorder threshold. Reporting & Documentation Generate weekly spare parts consumption and stock-position reports for the Lead, Inventory Support. Maintain a complete issuance log linking each spare part to its Job Card and technician. Track Part-Failure data to support procurement and OEM quality feedback. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain proper zoning, labelling, and cleanliness of the spare parts storage area at all times. Enforce segregation of duty: no self-authorised issuance. Support all scheduled and spot-check inventory counts. Requirements  Minimum of OND in a related discipline  At least 2-year experience in inventory operations. Good computer skills. Must know the Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word and PowerPoint)  Ability to work with limited supervision.  Strong attention to detail and accuracy. Proficiency in inventory management systems and workflow applications. Experience handling large volumes of items  Excellent organizational and record-keeping skills. Effective communication and stakeholder coordination. Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.

title: Inventory Support Officer - South South
description: Who We are Moniepoint Inc is a financial technology company digitizing Africa’s real economy by building a financial ecosystem for businesses, providing them with all the payment, banking, credit and business management tools they need to succeed.  What We do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community, dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We have several products that provide essential services for businesses such as credit, overdrafts etc. We leverage artificial intelligence and data to make our decisions but also have the technology and data-driven best practices used to support our businesses.  1A. Inventory Support Officer – POS Terminals Role Purpose The ISO (Terminals) is the dedicated custodian for all forms of POS terminals flowing through the repair pipeline. The role ensures end-to-end traceability, enforces custody controls, and maintains absolute logical–physical alignment within the Repair Centre's IMS subsystem, covering every stage from receipt of faulty units to dispatch of QA-cleared OK devices. Key Responsibilities Intake & Receipt Management Receive faulty/returned terminals from state offices; verify against the recall waybill at serial-number level before accepting into the IMS. Log all received devices in the IMS with correct status within 24 hours of physical arrival. Identify and quarantine damaged or missing-serial devices; raise a Discrepancy Report immediately. Repair Pipeline Tracking Push faulty devices to technicians daily and update IMS status to 'In Repair' upon assignment. Monitor movement of each terminal through all repair stages: Assessment → In Repair → Awaiting QA → QA Cleared → Dispatch Holding. Enforce the 24–72-hour SLA from receipt-to-assignment and from QA clearance-to-dispatch readiness. QA Integration & Status Management Receive QA-approved terminals and update IMS status to 'QA Cleared – Awaiting Dispatch' within 4 hours. Flag devices that fail QA back to the repair queue or classify as 'Beyond Economic Repair (BER)' with a written justification report. Ensure all 'BER' devices are tagged and isolated in the scrap/disposal holding area. Dispatch & Outbound Logistics Generate the Dispatch List and Waybill for QA-cleared refurbished and OK devices; obtain approval from Repair Centre Manager and Cluster lead before release. Scan all devices at serial level during physical loading; update IMS to 'In Transit – Outbound'. Confirm receipt acknowledgment from the destination state SIO and close the dispatch transaction in IMS. Inventory Counts & Reconciliation Conduct daily physical counts of all terminals in the repair centre; reconcile against IMS records. Escalate any variance (physical vs. logical) to the Lead, Inventory Support within the same business day. Participate in monthly, quarterly, and annual wall-to-wall counts as directed by the Inventory & Warehouse Manager. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain clearly labelled racks and segregated zones: Faulty, Under-Repair, Refurbished/OK, BER/Scrap. Enforce all provisions of the POS Inventory Control SOP within the repair centre. Uphold audit readiness, workplace safety, and environmental handling standards at all times. Reporting Line Functional: Lead, Inventory Support (Regional) Operational: Repair Centre Manager Dotted: Regional Inventory & Warehouse Manager   1B. Inventory Support Officer – Spare Parts Role Purpose The ISO (Spare Parts) manages the complete lifecycle of all repair consumables — batteries, screens, cables, and accessories — within the repair centre. The role ensures that technicians have the right parts at the right time, waste is minimised, and all issues are fully documented and traceable. Key Responsibilities Spare Parts Receipt & Storage Receive all incoming spare parts consignments; verify at batch/serial level against the accompanying delivery note before logging into IMS. Store spare parts in designated, labelled bins organised by part type and model compatibility. Ensure storage conditions protect electronic components from moisture, dust, and extreme temperature. Issuance Control Issue spare parts ONLY against an approved Job Card raised by a technician and validated by the Repair Centre Manager. Update IMS stock levels immediately upon every issuance; zero unrecorded movements. Manage parts returns from technicians (unused or incorrect parts); update IMS accordingly. Inventory Management & Reconciliation Reconcile physical spare parts stock against IMS records on a weekly basis. Identify slow-moving, expired, or obsolete parts and flag to Lead, Inventory Support. Raise a formal replenishment request when stock falls to the defined reorder threshold. Reporting & Documentation Generate weekly spare parts consumption and stock-position reports for the Lead, Inventory Support. Maintain a complete issuance log linking each spare part to its Job Card and technician. Track Part-Failure data to support procurement and OEM quality feedback. Compliance & Housekeeping Maintain proper zoning, labelling, and cleanliness of the spare parts storage area at all times. Enforce segregation of duty: no self-authorised issuance. Support all scheduled and spot-check inventory counts. Requirements  Minimum of OND in a related discipline  At least 2-year experience in inventory operations. Good computer skills. Must know the Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word and PowerPoint)  Ability to work with limited supervision.  Strong attention to detail and accuracy. Proficiency in inventory management systems and workflow applications. Experience handling large volumes of items  Excellent organizational and record-keeping skills. Effective communication and stakeholder coordination. Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.

title: Metadata & Data Lineage Specialist
description: Who we are  Moniepoint is an all-in-one digital financial services platform powering businesses across emerging markets. Since 2019, our technology has enabled over one million businesses to thrive through comprehensive payment, banking, credit, and business management solutions. Operating through its subsidiaries—including Moniepoint MFB and TeamApt Ltd—Moniepoint processes the majority of Nigeria's POS transactions, representing over $170 billion in annualised Total Payment Volume (TPV). Recognised as Africa’s second-fastest-growing fintech platform and named the Most Inclusive Payment Platform by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) in 2022, Moniepoint continues to scale its profitable financial ecosystem. About this role We are looking for a Metadata & Data Lineage Specialist to build out and run the organization's metadata management and data lineage capabilities. You will be the person who makes our data catalogue genuinely useful — helping teams find, trust, and understand the data they are working with, and tracing exactly how that data moves and transforms across our systems. You will take our metadata management and data lineage frameworks from paper to practice: growing coverage, improving quality, automating collection wherever possible, and building lineage that holds up for our most critical data products, regulatory submissions, and business-critical flows. Responsibilities Metadata Management & Data Cataloguing: Maintain and enhance enterprise metadata, developing business glossaries, data definitions, and ownership frameworks within DataHub. Identify gaps and ensure metadata changes align with governance processes. Data Lineage Management: Develop, maintain, and validate end-to-end data lineage for critical data flows, products, reports, and customer journeys across source systems, ETL/ELT pipelines, and downstream consumers. DataHub Platform & Integration: Support the administration and optimisation of DataHub. Configure ingestion workflows, monitor metadata ingestion jobs, and identify opportunities to improve coverage through automation and APIs. Metadata Quality & Governance: Establish metadata quality rules and KPIs. Perform regular assessments to highlight gaps, support data impact assessments, and ensure alignment with enterprise governance policies. Data Classification & Privacy: Apply data classification metadata based on sensitivity and regulatory requirements. Support Risk, Compliance, and InfoSec teams with necessary lineage information for assessments. AI & Advanced Data Discovery: Drive the adoption of AI-assisted metadata management to automate capture, classification, and enrichment. Contribute to the development of semantic models and knowledge graphs. Stakeholder Engagement: Act as a subject matter expert, facilitating workshops and providing guidance to data producers and consumers to improve overall data literacy and DataHub adoption. Experience & Background Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Management, Data Science, Information Systems, Library/Information Science, Engineering, or a related discipline. 3–6+ years of experience in Metadata Management, Data Governance, Data Architecture, or Data Engineering. Demonstrable hands-on experience with Solidatus, Informatica, DataHub, or a comparable enterprise data catalog platform. Practical experience developing end-to-end data lineage across complex data environments. Deep familiarity with modern data architectures (Medallion, Data Mesh, Data Vault 2.0, warehouses, data lakes, cloud platforms). Experience in financial services, fintech, payments, banking, or another highly regulated data environment is highly desirable. Skills & Competencies Strong proficiency working with technical and business metadata, business glossaries, data domains, and data classification. Experience working with relational databases and a solid understanding of SQL and database structures. Knowledge of APIs, ETL/ELT pipelines, and automated metadata integration. Familiarity with AI-assisted metadata management, semantic modelling, ontologies, and knowledge graph concepts. Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to facilitate training and influence adoption. Professional certification in Data Management or Architecture (e.g., DAMA CDMP, CIMP, DCAM) or related platform certifications are advantageous. What success looks like in this role The enterprise data catalogue is accurate, easily discoverable, and heavily utilised by cross-functional teams to understand data assets. End-to-end data lineage is robust, validated, and actively supports critical data products, regulatory submissions, and incident investigations. Metadata collection is highly automated, maintaining strict quality standards and governance controls with minimal manual intervention. Data literacy and platform adoption (DataHub) scale across the organisation through effective stakeholder enablement. What we can offer you Culture -We put our people first and prioritise the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter A technical interview with the hiring manager A behavioural and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.  Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

Job Title: Packaging Officer  Department: Repair Operations  Reports to: Regional Repair Operations Manager  Location: Rivers - Port Harcourt Work Mode: Onsite Employment Type: Outsourcing About this role:  The Packaging Officer is responsible for ensuring all refurbished terminals that pass quality assurance (QA) are properly packaged, labelled, and logged before being sent to inventory for distribution. What success looks like in this role: Consistently meeting or exceeding daily and weekly packaging output targets.  Maintaining a low return rate for packaged terminals by strictly adhering to quality criteria.  100% compliance with the packaging checklist and established SOPs.  High level of inventory accuracy with minimal logging discrepancies. title: Principal Mobile Engineer (POS Terminal)
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. About the role As a Principal Mobile Engineer (POS-Terminal) at Moniepoint, you will be responsible for designing and leading the architecture of our POS terminal solutions across multiple platforms. You will ensure the scalability, security, performance, and reliability of our POS systems and related applications, including mobile apps for repair scheduling and maintenance. While the majority of our terminals are currently based on Android Native, your expertise in cross-platform solutions (e.g., Flutter, C, JavaScript) will be crucial as we expand and diversify our portfolio.You’ll play a critical role in shaping the direction of our POS-related products, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and ensuring the technical vision aligns with the company’s broader strategic goals. Develop and maintain architectural documents and diagrams for POS terminal systems, ensuring all platforms are well documented and up to date. Make architectural decisions on POS terminal software, integrating various payment technologies, EMV standards, and ensuring hardware compatibility. Lead the development of POS-related applications Optimize system performance and security, particularly around payment processing and EMV protocols. Participate in planning sessions with product and engineering teams to ensure solutions meet market needs and business goals. Conduct code reviews and ensure best practices for mobile and embedded systems development, especially for Android Native development. Define and enforce software engineering best practices across the POS and related teams to improve efficiency and developer productivity. Provide technical mentorship to engineering teams, helping them grow their skills and contribute to the broader technical vision. To succeed in this role, we think you should have: At least 8 years of experience in system design, architecture, and development, specifically in the POS terminal domain. Strong expertise in Android Native development (Java/Kotlin), with a deep understanding of Android-based POS terminal solutions. Experience in cross-platform mobile development, such as Flutter, and familiarity with other POS application platforms (e.g., C, JavaScript) is a plus. Strong knowledge of EMV (Europay, Mastercard, and Visa) security protocols, including chip-based transactions, encryption, and key management. Experience with hardware integration for POS devices, such as card readers, pin pads, printers, and other peripherals. Deep understanding of payment systems architecture, including integration with payment processors and gateways. Knowledge of software quality assurance principles and their application in financial systems. Excellent problem-solving skills with an ability to manage complex system interactions and adapt to changing requirements. Strong communication skills, capable of presenting complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Leadership abilities with a focus on mentoring engineers and driving process improvements within the team. What we can offer you Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. title: Product Auditor
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. What We Do At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We leverage artificial intelligence and data-driven best practices to support our businesses, from providing credit and overdrafts to ensuring every transaction is secure. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Role Overview The Product Auditor provides independent assurance over the design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of product controls across payment, wallet, settlement, switches and other related products across the organisation The role ensures that new and existing products are deployed with adequate financial, operational, security, and regulatory controls, safeguarding the organization against revenue leakage, settlement failures, regulatory breaches, and technology-driven risks. The Product Auditor will independently evaluate product risk exposure and control maturity prior to scale. Key Responsibilities  Audit Universe & Risk-Based Planning Maintain a living Product Audit Universe covering all payment products, features, and integrations ranked by risk.  Own the annual Product Audit Plan, ensuring coverage is allocated dynamically based on risk ratings, product complexity, regulatory sensitivity, and change velocity. Product Design & Control Assurance Review PRDs, business rules, and transaction workflows to identify logic gaps, unmitigated risk paths, and missing exception-handling routines before products reach production/go-live.  Analyse product path scenarios, verify Maker-Checker enforcement, and provide formal control design sign-off before any material release goes live. Live Product Assessment ( Continuous Audit Review) Periodically assess live payment products to confirm they continue to operate within approved design parameters.  Detect configuration drift, identify silent divergence from original PRDs, and analyse live transaction data for emerging risk patterns. Go-Live Readiness & Control Gate Execute mandatory pre-production Product Audit reviews as an independent control gate for all material releases.  Confirm reconciliation logic, exception queues, and fallback controls are tested and functional.  Escalate critical deficiencies with risk ratings and hold recommendations where a product is not safe to release. Transaction Logic & Mathematical Integrity Interrogate the Fee Engine using SQL to mathematically prove that commissions, VAT, discounts, and splits are posted with complete precision.  Validate duplicate prevention mechanisms and ensure transaction integrity within complex, multi-step payment sequences, and test reversal, refund, and chargeback logic to confirm financial symmetry is maintained in every scenario. Settlement & Ledger Integrity Trace fund flows, confirming continuous synchronisation between wallet sub-ledgers and the General Ledger.  Assess reconciliation logic for breaks and evaluate the authorisation, documentation, and reversibility of manual settlement overrides. Product Change & Configuration Integrity Confirm that all product modifications: fee tables, routing rules, limit parameters passed through an approved change management cycle.  Identify silent changes made outside formal release processes and audit the integrity of product master data to ensure it is access-controlled, version-tracked, and consistent with approved product terms. Vendor & Third-Party Product Risk Assess controls over vendor-managed product components, evaluate SLA performance against contractual commitments, and identify single-vendor dependency risks within critical payment flows.  Evaluate the organisation's ability to detect unilateral changes in third-party API behaviour, fee logic, or settlement processes. Control Advisory & Stakeholder Engagement Engage product and engineering teams early in the design cycle to provide informal control advisory, reducing findings at the formal review stage without compromising independence.  Participate in design reviews and architecture discussions, and build a control-by-design culture across product teams.  Incident Review, RCA & Regulatory Alignment Lead post-incident reviews for product failures,producing structured RCA reports that identify underlying logic failures, not just surface symptoms.  Assess corrective actions for adequacy and track findings to verify closure.  Ensure product logic complies with CBN guidelines, PCI DSS, and consumer protection obligations at the design level, and evaluate the regulatory impact of new features before release. Reporting & Governance Prepare risk-rated audit reports for Executive Management and the Audit Committee, leading with findings, financial impact, and required action.  Maintain a Product Risk Register, deliver quarterly control maturity updates, and ensure governance bodies are never surprised by a product failure that was visible at the design or portfolio review stage. Required Knowledge & Skills  Technical Skills Advanced SQL for independent data extraction and transaction interrogation Payment systems architecture : Wallets, card processing, direct debit, settlement, and reconciliation API and integration literacy (Basic) End-to-end transaction lifecycle knowledge: Authorisation, posting, clearing, settlement, and exception handling PRD and process flow analysis: translating product documentation into control flowcharts Mathematical precision: fee calculations, interest computations, and split payment structures Pattern recognition: detecting anomalies, outliers, and irregularities in large transaction datasets Audit & Risk Skills Risk-based audit methodology: IIA Standards and COSO framework applied to financial products. Control design logic and evaluation Root cause analysis Regulatory knowledge: CBN payment system regulations, PCI DSS, NDPR,Nigerian consumer protection obligations etc Interpersonal & Professional Skills Stakeholder engagement Professional scepticism and independence Risk-rated report writing Tools & Platforms SQL (PostgreSQL / MySQL / MSSQL) AdvancedExcel / Google Sheets Claude / AI Tools Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Finance, or a related quantitative discipline Experience: 3–5+ years in Product Audit, Systems Audit, Financial Data Analytics, or Payment Operations within a fintech or financial services environment Certifications: CISA, CIA, or CFE preferred. ACA / ACCA is acceptable when combined with strong technical product experience and data analytics. Sector Knowledge: Demonstrated hands-on familiarity with payment product architecture, wallet systems, and regulated payment flows in a Nigerian or comparable market context. What We Offer You Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’re human, we listen, and we look out for one another. Learning: We’re big on growth. You’ll find an environment focused on knowledge sharing, training, and helping you reach your potential. Compensation: You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, and an annual bonus, along with other great benefits. What to Expect in the Hiring Process A preliminary phone call with our recruiter. An interview with the hiring team. A final conversation with a member of our executive team. Moniepoint Inc. is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Product Design Manager - Design System
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial ecosystem, helping 10 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, and business management tools since 2019. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, it powers most of the country’s Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Through its subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes $22 billion monthly for its customers while operating profitably. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. About the role  Designing for money means designing for trust. Our customers are shop owners, traders and entrepreneurs, and many are new to digital products. They work on low-end devices and unreliable networks, where one confusing screen can cost them a sale. Your team's work has to hold up for them, whatever their ability or device. You make sure it does.  As a Design Manager, you'll lead a small team of product designers and be accountable for everything they ship: its quality, how it works as one product, and the results it drives for our customers and the business. Your team works either on the products our customers use on POS, mobile and web, or on the operational tools our teams use to serve them.  It is a hands-on role: you build the systems the team works within and step into the hardest problems yourself.  What you'll do  Set the design direction for your area, turn it into plans with milestones and measurable outcomes, and make the case for it to senior leaders in customer and business terms. Work with product partners so every designer begins from a clear, well-framed brief, and push back early when one isn't ready.  Keep each customer journey whole across teams, and resolve conflicting designs before they launch.  Run critique and design reviews against a definition of done that includes accessibility, and stay close enough to the work that nothing reaches customers below the bar. Decide what must be tested with customers before build and what can ship and be measured after, and plan that validation into delivery with success metrics defined up front. Make sure journeys use the design system, with market and product variations handled inside it rather than as one-off rebuilds. Plan and staff system contributions like any other project. Build trusted partnerships with product and engineering, so design shapes what gets built, and design and engineering stay in step through build.  Hire well, set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and build a growth path for each designer.  Bring AI tools into the team's design process, model effective and responsible use in your own work, and build that fluency across the team.  What you'll need to succeed  10+ years of experience in product design, with a portfolio of shipped work across mobile and web that shows the problem, your decisions and the results.  3+ years of experience managing product designers, including hiring, coaching and career development.  Experience setting design direction for a product area and leading a team to deliver it. Experience running a design quality practice, such as critique, design reviews and a definition of done, that raised the quality of shipped work.  Experience building shared patterns or templates adopted across teams, products or markets. Experience shipping accessible, inclusive products for people with disabilities, people new to digital products and people on limited devices and connectivity.  Experience using AI tools in design work and building that fluency across a team.  Nice to have  Experience designing for POS terminals is a strong plus. Experience in financial services, multiple markets or operational tools is also welcome.  What you will get: A leadership role in shaping the future of fintech - your work will impact millions of users. Career growth opportunities. A culture of experimentation - we encourage innovative thinking and rapid iteration. Competitive compensation and benefits. Remote-friendly work culture, with access to learning resources. What to expect in the hiring process  Recruiter conversation. Your background, what you want next, and practical details. 2. Case study review. Walk a design leader through one or two case studies in depth: one from your own work, one from a team you led.  Leadership challenge. Work through a product and team problem live with two design leaders.  Final interview. A conversation with the hiring manager. Why Join Us Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities. Fully remote work culture and support for professional development. What to expect in the hiring process Application & portfolio review: we assess your experience, leadership impact, and Design System case studies that demonstrate strategic thinking, process, and measurable outcomes. Preliminary phone call with recruiter: a brief conversation to discuss your background, leadership experience, and expectations. Interview with senior leadership: a deep dive into your leadership approach, design philosophy, and ability to drive impact. This includes a discussion on past projects and collaboration with cross-functional teams. Design leadership challenge: a scenario-based assessment to assess both strategic thinking and leadership skills while balancing UX/UI expertise. Final executive conversation: a discussion with senior leadership to assess alignment with our vision, strategic thinking, and team-building philosophy. How to apply: Submit your resume and portfolio showcasing your leadership in managing design teams, driving strategy, and delivering user-centred solutions with measurable business impact. We want to see case studies that demonstrate how you have led and developed designers, prioritised and managed projects, and fostered a high-performing team culture. Your portfolio should highlight how you have used research, data, and experimentation to inform decisions, optimise workflows, and drive success metrics.
